title: QuickFlow starter kit — sketch
content:
Context:
A compact, opinionated set of prebuilt conversational flows (QuickFlows) that product teams can drop into their web/mobile assistants to speed time-to-first-value. Aim: reduce engineering lift for common flows (onboarding, task capture, clarifying Qs, fallback recovery), provide sensible defaults for token budgets, telemetry hooks, and guardrails while keeping customization simple.

Why now:
- Customers repeatedly ask for reference flows + copy for quick demos and internal pilots.
- Onboarding cost of an LLM-powered assistant is often UX copy + fallback logic + instrumentation — lots of repeated work across teams.
- If we ship starter kit, we lower time-to-success and create a standardized surface for Optimize to recommend quantization/cost settings per-flow.

Core idea (top-level):
- QuickFlow = small JSON-y manifest + optional UI snippets + SDK glue.
- Each QuickFlow includes: intent schema, minimal prompt templates, recommended model/temperature, token budget guidance, fallback policy, telemetry events, and sample UI copy.
- Provide ~6 starter QuickFlows: welcome/onboarding, short Q&A, task-capture (todo/booking), clarification-dialog, graceful-fallback, and summary/recap.

User stories (rough):
- As a PM, I want a drop-in welcome flow to onboard users to the assistant in 1 day, so I can run a pilot.
- As an engineer, I want SDK helpers that wire telemetry and rate limits automatically, so I don't write boilerplate for each flow.
- As an SRE, I want per-flow token budget and an autoscale hint so we can predict cost spikes and route heavy flows to Dedicated.
- As a design writer, I want sample microcopy and variant A/B text so I can test conversion quickly.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Repo with 6 QuickFlow manifests + sample UI snippets (React + mobile pseudo-code).
- SDK helper: instantiateQuickFlow(flowManifest, {user, session}) -> renders prompts + emits telemetry events.
- Console surface: per-flow telemetry (invocations, avg tokens, p99 latency) + toggle to pin model recommendation.
- One customer pilot onboarded (internal beta) and feedback collected.

Metrics to watch:
- Time to integrate (target <1 day for dev to show demo).
- Average tokens per flow, tokens saved after Optimize recommendations.
- Pilot conversion: % teams that move from pilot to production within 60 days.
- Error rate for fallbacks and user drop-off after fallback.

Implementation notes / tech constraints:
- Flow manifest schema must be lightweight and versioned (v0.1 for MVP). Keep fields: id, name, intents[], prompt_templates{start, followup, clarification}, recommended_model, safety_filters, token_budget, fallback_policy_id, telemetry_events[]. No deep nested JSON (keep simple).
- SDK should be small JS package (tree-shakable) with 2 core helpers: bindFlowToElement and flowRunner. FlowRunner handles session state + KV caching.
- Telemetry events: flow.start, flow.step, flow.fallback, flow.complete with token counts. Console must pick these up without extra instrumentation.
- Default token budget suggestions per flow based on typical median + p90 from hosted-api benchmarks (we'll start with conservative defaults).

Rollout plan (phases):
- Phase 0 (now): internal hackday prototype + design writer drafts.
- Phase 1 (2 weeks): MVP manifests + SDK + internal beta with 3 product teams.
- Phase 2 (4–6 weeks): polish manifests, add Console per-flow page, build QuickFlow catalog page, document integration guide.
- Phase 3: public beta + sample templates in quickstart.

Open questions / risks:
- How opinionated should prompts be? We risk leakage of brand voice vs too-generic flows. Start conservative: provide 2 voice variants (neutral, friendly).
- Fallback policy design: best-effort vs strict failover to cheaper model. Need safety review for auto-downgrading.
- Metrics privacy: telemetry will include token counts tied to user ids for billing — ensure PII not included in events.
- Model pinning and Dedicated routing: how to expose autoscale hints in manifest without leaking infra details.

Prototype TODOs (next actions):
- [ ] Draft manifest schema doc in repo (Mira).
- [ ] Build quick React demo page to show welcome flow (Ava).
- [ ] Wire basic telemetry events to Console (Hugo).
- [ ] Create copy variants and an A/B experiment plan.
- [ ] Create a small pilot checklist for solutions engineering: integration steps, expected telemetry, rollback plan.

Notes to self / heuristics:
- Keep starters tiny: 3–5 prompts per flow, include a canned 'help' fallback line, explicit user-confirmation step before any destructive action.
- Recommend default temperature 0.2 for task flows, 0.7 for creative Q&A.
- Token budget: provide 'soft' and 'hard' budgets; SDK should allow soft enforcement (warn + telemetry) and hard enforcement (truncate + fallback).

Example manifest snippet (illustrative, not final):
- id: quickflow-welcome-v0
- name: "Welcome — quick start"
- intents: ["greeting","onboard-optin"]
- prompt_templates.start: "Hi {first_name}! I can help with X. Want a quick tour?"
- recommended_model: "redwood-llama-13b-q4"
- token_budget: {soft: 150, hard: 512}  <-- SDK will store as ints, expose in Console

Slack / ticket refs to link in doc: quickflow-discuss in #product-hack, ping @mira for manifest questions.

Good to ship if we can show a 1-day demo flow to a product stakeholder and have the SDK emit the 4 telemetry events with sensible token counts.

Parking lot ideas (nice-to-have later):
- Flow composer UI in Console to edit prompts + copy and preview tokens in real time.
- Marketplace of community contributed QuickFlows with vetting.
- Auto-suggested prompt templates from existing customer logs (privacy-safe aggregated patterns).
- Built-in quality eval harness for each QuickFlow to detect regressions on small eval suites.

End-of-note.

---
Short changelog: created 2024-11-03, sketch updated with collaborator notes 2024-11-09.
